title: Wirtschaftsindex der Chicago-Fed steigt im August
content: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index (CFNAI) rose to minus 0.12 in August, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago. The index for July was revised to minus 0.28 from an earlier figure of minus 0.19. The three‑month moving average improved to minus 0.18 in August, with July’s revised value at minus 0.20 instead of the previously reported minus 0.18. A CFNAI of zero signals growth at the historical trend level; a negative reading indicates expansion below that trend, while a positive reading would show growth above it.

title: Wirtschaftsindex der Chicago-Fed sinkt im Juli
content: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index (CFNAI) fell to minus 0.19 in July, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago. The index for June was revised to minus 0.18 from an earlier figure of minus 0.10. The three‑month moving average rose to minus 0.18 in July, after being revised to minus 0.26 for June (previously minus 0.28). A CFNAI of zero indicates growth at the historical trend level; a negative value signals growth below the trend, while a positive value indicates growth above the trend.

content: The Chicago Fed’s National Activity Index (CFNAI) recorded a reading of –0.12 in August, the highest level in five months, after a revision from –0.28 in July. The index indicates a modest uptick in economic growth. Production‑related activity rose to –0.02 from –0.17 in July. Sales, orders and inventory contributed a neutral reading, improving from –0.02. Employment‑related activity increased to –0.07 from –0.10. Personal consumption and housing fell to –0.03 from 0.02. The three‑month moving average (CFNAI‑MA3) climbed from –0.20 to –0.18.

content: The U.S. economic activity index, the Chicago Fed National Activity Index (CFNAI), rose to **-0.12** in August, up from **-0.28** in July (revised from an initial **-0.19**). This reading is higher than the market expectation of **-0.16**. The three‑month moving average improved from **-0.20** (revised from **-0.18**) to **-0.18**. Historically, periods of economic expansion have been associated with CFNAI values above **-0.35**.

title: Chicago Fed's NAI Increased in August, Stayed Negative
content: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index (NAI) rose to minus 0.12 in August, up from minus 0.28 in July, according to the Fed’s monthly report. Its three‑month moving average improved to minus 0.18 from minus 0.20 a month earlier. Production, employment, personal consumption and housing all made negative contributions to the headline index, while the sales, orders and inventories category was neutral.

title: Chicago PMI ekonomik yavaşlamayı işaret etti Yazar ForInvest Haber
content: The Chicago Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) fell to 41.5 in August from 47.1 in July, dropping below the 50‑point threshold that separates expansion from contraction and signalling a slowdown in economic activity. Economists had expected the PMI to rise to 47.3. The decline comes amid persistent price pressures in the U.S. economy, which is increasing pressure on the Federal Reserve to cut rates. Despite July’s unchanged annual inflation according to the Fed‑preferred consumer price index, the new PMI reading is likely to intensify calls for rate cuts at the upcoming policy meeting.

title: Índice de atividade nacional dos EUA sobe a -0,12 em agosto
content: According to a survey released by the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago on Monday, September 22 2025, the U.S. national activity index rose to –0.12 in August from –0.28 in July. The July figure was revised downward from –0.19. The three‑month moving average of the index increased from –0.20 in July to –0.18 in August. Although the index remains below zero, the improvement indicates that the U.S. economy continues to expand, albeit at a pace below its historical average.
